title: Multipart function-call retries can reorder parameters across proxy reconnects
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted, Dedicated, and Private/VPC) have reported structured-output corruption when using multipart streaming function/tool calls. The failure occurs after a proxy reconnect or retry: fragments of the multipart payload are sometimes reordered or duplicated, causing the function-invoke layer to assemble parameters incorrectly and resulting in malformed JSON passed to customer tools. This manifests as 400s from tool endpoints, incorrect tool-selection decisions, and occasionally downstream data corruption in single-tenant Dedicated deployments.

Why this is urgent: Two enterprise customers on Dedicated and one private deployment experienced production failures for customer-visible features (document ingestion and order processing). Because retries occur under network flaps, outages can cascade and customers see degraded availability. We marked P0 due to repeated escalations and impact on SLAs for Dedicated customers.

Distinguishing notes: Unlike prior stream-framing or delimiter mis-detection issues, this bug is specifically caused by race between proxy-side buffered retry logic and the runtime's multipart sequencer when connection state is re-established. It is not a parser bug alone — it is a sequencing/idempotency gap introduced by reconnection and replay behavior in the proxy path (both hosted-side proxy and customer-side private proxies).
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy a model with streaming function/tool-calling enabled and structured JSON params that exceed a single frame
Introduce a network interruption on the proxy (simulate TCP connection close mid-stream) or trigger a proxy retry via fault injection
Allow the client to reconnect quickly and let the proxy resend buffered frames without strict sequence ids
Observe assembled function invocation at the runtime: parameter order changes, duplicated parameter segments, or shifted JSON boundaries leading to parse errors or incorrect tool invocation
observed_behavior: When a proxy reconnect and resend happens, multipart frame segments can arrive out of original order. The runtime's sequencer sometimes treats resent frames as new segments rather than deduplicating by sequence id, causing parameter reordering or duplication in the reconstructed payload. Customers see tool invocation failures, JSON parse errors, and inconsistent outputs across retries.
expected_behavior: The runtime should reconstruct multipart streams deterministically even if the proxy reconnects and resends buffered frames: resent frames must be deduplicated and applied in original sequence order using robust sequence ids and connection-scoped session tags. Structured output parsers should only see a single coherent payload per logical invocation.
root_cause: Race between proxy retry/resend and runtime's session lifecycle. The proxy (hosted side and some customer private proxies) currently resends buffered frames on reconnect without preserving a globally unique message sequence id per logical invocation. The runtime's multipart sequencer relies on ephemeral per-connection counters; on reconnect it assigns a new connection scope and accepts resent frames as new ones. This creates an idempotency gap where duplicates are accepted instead of discarded, and segment ordering is not enforced across reconnects.
proposed_fix:
1) Enhance wire protocol: attach a stable invocation_id + segment_seq to every multipart frame so frames are globally addressable across reconnects. 2) Update runtime sequencer to track seen (invocation_id, segment_seq) pairs for a grace window and discard duplicates. 3) Add connection-reconnect handshake where proxy sends last-acked-seq for active invocations to allow re-sync. 4) Add defensive parser checks for overlapping JSON boundaries and fail fast with clear error codes.

Implementation will be authored in two parts: protocol schema change + runtime sequencer change. We will ship backward-compatible parsing that falls back when clients are older, with a runtime-side guard to avoid accepting frames that appear to be duplicates without an invocation_id.
rollforward_plan: Merge PRs into release branch (runtime-1.22) after automated integration tests. Roll out to hosted canary (5% traffic) for 48 hours, monitor tool error rate and structured-output parse errors. On success, gradually increase to 100% over 72 hours. For Dedicated and Private customers: provide a small agent update (v1.22) and recommend rolling update of sidecar proxies. Coordinate with SEs to schedule low-risk maintenance windows for enterprise tenants.
rollback_plan: If we detect increased errors or new regressions during canary, revert runtime changes and re-enable previous sequencing behavior. For Dedicated/Private, we can pin to prior runtime binary and instruct customers to roll back proxy agent to previous stable version. Maintain feature-flag gate to disable new dedup window if needed.
tests: Unit tests for sequencer dedup discard logic
Integration test that simulates reconnect + resend and verifies deterministic reconstruction
Load test to ensure dedup tracking memory bounds under high concurrency
E2E test with Private deployment (VPC) including common customer proxy configurations
Mutation tests to ensure parser fail-fast behavior for overlapping JSON segments
comments: 2025-02-10 Asha Patel: Ticket created after initial SE escalation from customer AcmeRetail (Dedicated) and internal monitoring spike. Captured sample request traces and initial pcap from customer VPC proxy.
2025-02-11 Marcus Liu: Reproduced locally with fault-injector. Confirmed reorder when proxy reconnects mid-stream. Began PoC to include invocation_id in frames.
2025-02-12 Zoe Kim (SRE): Added Grafana dashboard panel to track multipart parse errors and invocation_id absence. Alert created for >5 errors/min.
2025-02-14 Marcus Liu: Opened PRs for sequencer and proxy changes. Preliminary unit tests added. Noted memory growth when dedup window is unbounded — added bounded LRU plan.

2025-02-16 SE Team (Jared Morales): Communicated mitigations to affected customers: increased client-side retry backoff and recommended rolling update of sidecar proxies to latest beta in staging. Customer scheduled maintenance window for 2025-02-20.
2025-02-18 Marcus Liu: Integration tests pass in CI. Starting hosted canary rollout at 10:00 UTC 2025-02-18. Monitoring toolcall error rate closely.
